topic: What if you could grow at will? Part 2
title: PART 2
THE WORD

power.rule: one word, and you get bigger, as big as you like
power.look: a gold pulse from the feet, eyes lit gold, a height ruler climbing to ×10, a GROW chip; a low swell snapping up into a springy overshoot

length_note: Part 2 of the long cut, continuing from Part 1's cliffhanger; Parts 1 and 2 play back to back (about 2 min 20 s).

script.beat: 1 cold open: the run up the stairs
script.text: You run. Crutch first, every stair. Her door won't open. Because her room isn't a room anymore.
Your little sister is the size of the house. And she loves it. She laughs, and every window on the street rattles.
Here's what you didn't know: the word works for anyone who hears it.
She waves at the whole street. Mum faints. Twice. She picks up the cat, very gently.

script.beat: 4 the turn: a new cost, one real fact, worked out
script.text: Then she sways. Blood is heavy. At ten times her height, her heart has to push it ten times higher. That takes about three times the pressure her heart can make. And without blood, a brain switches off in about ten seconds. That's real.
Ten seconds. There's only one way to catch her. You say the word. Your leg isn't healed. You do it anyway.
Nine. Eight. You catch her. Then you both sit down, and wait. Slowly, the street gets bigger again.
Across the street, the man in the suit isn't calling for help. He's filming. Everything.

script.beat: 7 cliffhanger, a question for the comments
script.text: The next morning, there's a card on your pillow. One word on it. And it isn't grow.

science.claim: At ten times her height, her heart has to push blood ten times higher; that takes about three times the pressure her heart can make.
science.working: The pressure needed to lift a column of blood is rho g h. Her brain sits about 0.3 m above her heart; at x10 that is 3 m: 1,060 kg/m3 x 9.81 m/s2 x 3 m = 31 kPa = about 235 mmHg, just to get blood up to her brain. A child's mean arterial pressure is about 75 to 85 mmHg: roughly a third of what she would need, so 'about three times the pressure her heart can make'.
science.source: Hydrostatic pressure (rho g h); blood density about 1,060 kg/m3; paediatric blood pressure norms. For scale: a giraffe, built for it, runs at about twice our pressure to lift blood some 2 m.

science.claim: Without blood, a brain switches off in about ten seconds.
science.working: When blood flow to the brain stops, consciousness is lost within about 5 to 10 seconds.
science.source: R. Rossen, H. Kabat, J. P. Anderson, 'Acute arrest of cerebral circulation in man', Archives of Neurology and Psychiatry, 1943 (loss of consciousness after a mean of about 6.8 s).
